entities.summary:
Luca Ghini (luca-ghini) was an Italian physician and botanist, born in the late 15th century, who created the first recorded herbarium, as well as the first botanical garden in Europe, in Bologna, Italy (Italy).





 Ghini's work on plant classification and his establishment of the botanical garden had a significant impact on the development of botany and horticulture in Europe during the Renaissance.










 Ghini's herbarium, which included over 1,000 plant specimens, served as a valuable resource for future botanists and scientists, contributing to the advancement of botanical knowledge and the understanding of plant classification.










 Luca Ghini's legacy can be seen in the many botanical gardens and herbaria that followed in his footsteps, including the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, in England, which was founded in the 17th century and continues to be a major center for botanical research and conservation.
